connections.why: Studying modern poetry alongside pre-1900 poetry builds the cross-period sensitivity to form and tone needed for unseen verse
Analysing modern drama develops the understanding of dramatic form and genre extended to Shakespeare
Pre-1900 prose and Shakespeare share the demand for historically informed close reading of older language
Reading pre-1900 prose deepens the contextual grasp required for pre-1900 poetry
Genre awareness from Shakespeare informs how students read the conventions of earlier poetry
The independent close-reading instinct honed on unseen poetry underpins the self-directed NEA
Sustained essay-writing on prose models the extended independent analysis demanded by the internal assessment
The genre and contextual frameworks from the Shakespeare unit feed the critical approaches used in coursework
